input: Make a short travel film from old footage

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which trips, destinations, or time periods to include determines how much material is in play and whether the film tells one story or many.
The target duration of the final film shapes every editing decision — pacing, how many clips to use, and how much to cut.
Whether the film is for a personal keepsake, a social media audience, a gift, or a public showcase completely changes tone, privacy considerations, and content choices.
The platform or setting where it will be shown (Instagram, YouTube, a family gathering, etc.) affects aspect ratio, length limits, and style expectations.
What editing software or tools the user has access to determines what guidance or workflow is actually actionable for them.
The desired mood and style — cinematic and emotional vs. fun and upbeat vs. documentary-style — drives music choice, color grading, and editing rhythm.
Understanding whether the user wants a polished, shareable final cut or simply a personal memento sets the quality bar and effort level for the whole project.

gold.taskTitle: Edit a short travel film from old footage
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to compile and edit existing travel footage into a short film.

questions.title: Which trips or destinations should the film cover?
questions.description: Identify the specific travel footage to include — one trip, multiple trips, a particular time period, or a specific theme.

questions.title: How long should the finished film be?
questions.description: Pin down the target runtime — for example, under 60 seconds, 2–3 minutes, or 5+ minutes — to guide all pacing and editing decisions.

questions.title: Who is the intended audience for this film?
questions.description: Clarify whether it is a personal keepsake, a gift for someone specific, or content made for a broader audience.

questions.title: Where will the film be shared or screened?
questions.description: Determine the platform or setting — Instagram Reels, YouTube, a family event, a personal hard drive — as this affects format and technical specs.

questions.title: What editing software do you currently have available?
questions.description: Find out the tools at hand — such as CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, iMovie, Premiere Pro — to tailor the workflow to what is actually usable.

questions.title: What mood or style should the film feel like?
questions.description: Establish the creative direction — cinematic and emotional, light and fun, slow and reflective, action-packed — to guide music, pacing, and color choices.

questions.title: What would make you feel this film turned out well?
questions.description: Understand the user's quality bar — a rough personal memento is fine, or it needs to feel polished enough to proudly share publicly.
